name: Huesca (Spain)
description: Square red flag with a white indented border, charged with a red saltire over a complex geometric pattern of yellow and green, with the arms of Huesca (VV OSCA) at the centre.
history: The present flag of Huesca is owed to Philip V, who on suppressing the fueros of Aragon granted Huesca a new flag; the city had until then its own flag, that of the Guardian Angel watching over the city. The present flag is composed of the cross of Saint Andrew, on which the apostle was martyred, and a series of complex geometric motifs in white, red, yellow and green, with the Roman motto VV OSCA at the centre.
